points: 1 Architecture and pretraining: 14B decoder-only model, nearly the same as phi-3-medium. Changes: tiktoken tokenizer with a padded vocabulary of 100,352, and full attention over 4K instead of a 2K sliding window. About 10T pretraining tokens, peak LR 0.0003, weight decay 0.1, batch 5760 (p. 7).

2 Synthetic-data recipe: 50 dataset types, about 400B unweighted tokens. Techniques: curated web, book and code seeds; majority-vote question filtering that drops all-agree and all-disagree questions; QA extraction from deduction chains; rewriting; self-revision; instruction reversal; execution-based validation (pp. 5-6).

3 Pretraining mix and how it was chosen. Table 5: synthetic 40%, web 15%, web rewrites 15%, code 20%, acquired 10%, with unique tokens and epochs (synthetic 13.8 epochs). A 13B synthetic-only model trails phi-3-medium on TQA (-14.8). In the 7B/1T-token ablations, synthetic-heavy mixes score marginally better, but web data is kept for knowledge (pp. 8-10).

4 Midtraining and long context: 4K to 16K over 250B tokens, RoPE base 250K, LR cut 10x, 30% long-context data plus 70% recall data. HELMET results at 8K/16K against Qwen-2.5-14B, Llama-3.3-70B, GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o (pp. 10-12).

5 Post-training recipe: SFT on about 8B tokens at LR 1e-6, including 40 languages. DPO round 1 uses Pivotal Token Search pairs. DPO round 2 is judge-guided: about 850k pairs from GPT-4o, GPT-4t and phi-4 responses, judged by GPT-4o (p. 12).

6 Pivotal Token Search mechanism: estimate p(success|prefix) with rollouts checked by an oracle; recursively bisect to find single tokens that shift p(success) by at least p_gap; build single-token accepted/rejected DPO pairs on the shared prefix; keep only questions with 0.2 <= p(success) <= 0.8 (pp. 14-16).
7 Post-training ablation (Table 9): PTS-DPO helps most on GPQA and MATH, judge-guided DPO helps most on ArenaHard, and the two are called complementary. Final GPQA is 56.1 vs 47.3 after SFT (p. 16).

8 Headline results (Table 1, simple-evals): GPQA 56.1 and MATH 80.4, both above teacher GPT-4o (50.6 / 74.6). phi-4 wins 9 of 12 benchmarks against Qwen-2.5-14B-Instruct and trails it on SimpleQA, DROP and IFEval. IFEval is admitted as a real weakness (pp. 1-3, 18).

9 Contamination and evaluation controls: fresh November 2024 AMC-10/12 tests (100 runs, t=0.5); improved, n-gram-based decontamination that the authors admit misses rephrasings; reliance on PhiBench, an internal benchmark also used for tuning (pp. 3, 16-18).

10 What is withheld: training compute and hardware, the models that generated the synthetic data, the p_gap value, DPO hyperparameters, and PhiBench contents. Safety is reported only on in-house RAI benchmarks (Table 10) plus AIRT red-teaming (pp. 18-19).
